Sclerotinia also shows plant collapse on black plastic mulch — another strong candidate. One view left.

Gray_Mold shows microscopy — not relevant. All 16 views complete.

**Summary of evidence:**

| Class | Key observation |
|---|---|
| Bacterial_Wilt (Bugwood_6) | Black plastic mulch, complete wilt, plants still somewhat upright/staked |
| Southern_Blight (Bugwood_5) | Complete prostrate collapse on plastic mulch — closest to test image posture |
| Southern_Blight (Bugwood_13) | Black plastic mulch, lower stem wilt |
| Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot (Bugwood_2) | Black plastic mulch, severe branch collapse |

**Decision rationale:**
The test image shows a tomato plant completely prostrate (lying flat) on black plastic mulch with pale green leaves still attached but fully wilted. This complete collapse — rather than drooping-while-upright — is most characteristic of crown/stem rot at the soil line (Southern Blight, Sclerotium rolfsii), which rots the stem base causing the whole plant to fall over suddenly while leaves are still green. The Bugwood_5 reference image shows this exact prostrate-on-mulch collapse pattern. Bacterial_Wilt reference (Bugwood_6) matched the black plastic setting but showed plants hanging wilted rather than fully prostrate.
